findings.finding: Path-based surface detection in `_surface_detect.py` with string rules (excluding singular `route`/`router`) is heuristic and repo-calibrated. The BRIEF says the verifier "re-derives from the diff," and this satisfies it, but path heuristics will misclassify renames (e.g., a new file named `routes.py` under a tooling dir vs. a real API route added inside an existing handler file with no path signal), and any false negative is a bypass — the exact bug this unit exists to fix.
findings.suggestion: Document the known-blind-spot set (changes inside an already-surface-touched file whose path alone doesn't indicate it, e.g., edits to an existing route handler body when the file isn't name-matched) in the module docstring and, if cheap, add a content-level signal (e.g., decorator scan `@app.route|@router|websocket|emit`) for non-excluded files. If content scanning is out of scope, at minimum note it as a residual risk in the unit notes.

findings.finding: _surface_evidence.py` failing on "fewer passes than `tests_run`" and "a runner-named test path without a passing result" conflates evidence-index coverage with per-path bookkeeping. Depending on how `fresh_evidence` records results (aggregated vs. per-path), the per-path check may be under-specified here and is the most likely source of false failures on legitimately passing runs.
findings.suggestion: Before writing code, confirm the evidence index actually records per-test-path results; if it only records suite-level counts, drop or weaken the per-path check rather than inventing a mapping, and note it.

findings.finding: "head_commit not an ancestor of the verified commit" — if the verified commit is head, or the branch was rebased (evidence produced on a commit that was subsequently rebased away but content-identical), the ancestor check will fail stale evidence that is arguably valid. Also unhandled: no merge-base case (unrelated histories) and shallow clones.
findings.suggestion: Decide and test: same-commit evidence is valid; rebased evidence fails (acceptable strictness, but say so); merge-base failure = unmeasurable = fail closed. Add these as explicit test cases.

findings.finding: The `none` refusal path handles "unmeasurable diff or non-git tree" by refusing — good — but `commit_hash=""` is the default in the moved `check_surface_verification`. Other call sites (or older saved scripts) that don't pass the commit will silently take the unmeasurable path and fail everything at medium+, a behavior change for existing callers.
findings.suggestion: Audit all `run_all_checks`/direct callers of the check to ensure commit is threaded through; consider making `commit_hash` required (no default) to fail loudly at integration time rather than at medium+ runs.

findings.finding: Moving `check_surface_verification` out of `iterate_checks.py` with re-export is the right call per the bloat cap, but "net lines <= 0 (grandfathered at 463; argparse compacted)" invites contorting the producer CLI to hit a line budget. Compacting argparse at the cost of readable flags/error messages is over-optimization of a metric.
findings.suggestion: Keep the compaction honest — helper-table argparse patterns are fine; don't degrade `--help` or error messages to shave lines. If the cap can't be met cleanly, raise it in the plan rather than distort the code.

findings.finding: Deleting superseded positive-path tests in `test_verify_iterate_finalization.py` (at cap) while adding coverage in new files is fine, but the plan doesn't mention checking that nothing else imports the moved check from `iterate_checks` (re-export covers it, but only if it's a true re-export of the same symbol including default-arg behavior change).
findings.suggestion: Add a grep/import check for `check_surface_verification` across the repo and scripts as a step in the mini-plan.

findings.finding: Closed-vocab `surface_none` codes include `no-startable-surface`, which seems to overlap with the diff-based detection refusing `none` when a surface is touched. If detection says a runnable surface is touched but the reason code is `no-startable-surface`, the two rules disagree — which wins isn't specified.
findings.suggestion: Specify precedence explicitly (detection wins; the reason code is only a claim) and test the conflict case.

findings.finding: Accepting evidence when `head_commit` is an ancestor of the verified commit allows stale evidence through. Tests from commit A remain acceptable after commit B changes the surface, provided the run ID matches.
findings.suggestion: Require evidence for the exact verified revision, or prove that the tested tree matches it using an existing tree/content identity mechanism. Test same-run evidence from an ancestor followed by a surface change.

findings.finding: Path-only detection, particularly the explicit exclusion of singular `route`/`router` names, leaves a practical bypass. Real API handlers commonly use these names, and message contracts can live in ordinary model files. Calibration against this tooling repository does not establish coverage for application repositories.
findings.suggestion: Use project/framework context and relevant diff content to distinguish tooling dispatch from runnable routes and contracts. Treat ambiguous executable changes conservatively. Add representative application fixtures, including `route.ts`, `router.py`, and a contract change outside a specially named directory.

findings.finding: The proposed evidence checks establish passing results and counts, but do not explicitly bind those results to the detected surface. A Playwright report selected because the block claims `web`, or unrelated passing tests satisfying `tests_run`, does not meet the stated contract. Leaving `cli` versus detected UI entirely unchecked preserves this gap.
findings.suggestion: Derive evidence requirements from detected surface kinds and require corresponding staged runner results. This can remain a verifier-only change without expanding producer-side detection. Test detected UI with a `cli` claim and only CLI evidence, plus API/realtime changes with unrelated passing tests.  The extraction and fail-closed direction are sound and proportionate. Revision freshness, detection coverage, and evidence-to-surface binding need explicit fixes before this satisfies U5.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

[glm] ## Findings

**Category: bug — Severity: medium**
File: `shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_surface_evidence.py` (`_revision_problem`)
The loop `for later in out.split()[1:]` unconditionally skips the first commit in `head..commit` on the assumption that `[0]` is the F6 commit — i.e., that evidence was staged at the pre-F6 trunk tip. But the repair guidance (and `stage_f0_evidence.py` usage shown in `_STAGE`) stages with `--head-commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`, which is frequently the F6 commit itself (or later). In that case `[0]` in `head..commit` is the *next* commit, and a code-changing commit immediately after the staging point escapes the staleness check entirely — exactly the bypass this unit exists to close. The one test that exercises the post-commit sequence (`test_a_code_commit_after_the_f6_commit_makes_the_evidence_stale`) always stages at the trunk tip, so it never covers this shape.
Suggestion: only skip `[0]` when it is demonstrably the F6 commit (e.g. skip only commits whose diff is records-only, or record the tested tree commit in the provenance sidecar and compare against it); add a test that stages at the F6 commit and then lands a code fix.
